#!/bin/sh
set -e
goal="Rename stores to model, maintaining coherence"
echo "Plan:"
echo "1. Rename src/frontend/stores to src/frontend/model"
echo "2. Update any references to the old path in code to prevent breakage"

# Rename src/frontend/stores to src/frontend/model
mv src/frontend/stores src/frontend/model

# Find and replace all occurrences of "stores" with "model" in the src/frontend directory
find src/frontend -type f -name '*.js' -o -name '*.jsx' -exec sed -i '' 's/stores/model/g' {} +

echo "\033[32mDone: $goal\033[0m\n"

conversations.answer: The issue in the original script is that the find command was only looking for files with the .js and .jsx extensions. The remaining references could be in other file types or in paths that weren't caught by the find command.To fix this, we need to modify the find command to search all text files in the specified directory.Here's the corrected script:[CODE_BLOCK_0]The -exec grep -Iq . {} \; part of the command checks if the file is a text file. It will now find and replace occurrences of "stores" in all text files within the src/frontend directory, not just those with specific extensions.
